body: Welcome back to The Card — I'm Matt Manzella, and this is the one desk on this site where we talk about the numbers that move money. This is Partner Content, presented by Kalshi, the regulated exchange where you trade on game outcomes instead of betting against a house. The rule here has not changed: every number below traces to a named source, every position gets logged in public, and there are no locks and no guarantees. Tonight's game is the Kansas City Chiefs (8-2) at the Buffalo Bills (9-1), Thursday, Nov. 26 at 8:20 PM ET at Highmark Stadium on NBC — the first Thanksgiving home game in Bills history, with the AFC's No. 1 seed on the table. And the most honest price in this matchup is not the spread. It is the total, and it has fallen five points.

Start with the headline prices. Buffalo is a 3-point home favorite with a game total of 45.5, per NBC Sports' Thanksgiving Day odds page, which lists the moneyline at Bills -151 and Chiefs +127 via DraftKings. That total is the story: the game opened at 50.5, per Sports Illustrated's opening-odds report, and the opening spread was Buffalo -2.5, per USA TODAY's picks page. A spread that barely moves while a total sheds five points is the market telling a specific story — it still believes this is a close game between equals, but it no longer believes it gets played in the 50s. On Kalshi, Buffalo is priced at 58 percent to win with the total set at 47.5, per Covers' Nov. 26 morning update — a higher total than the sportsbooks are hanging, and a gap worth noticing before kickoff.

Wednesday's final injury report is the first reason the total fell. Buffalo listed five players as questionable, per the Bills' official injury report: cornerback Christian Benford (groin), tight end Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle), right guard O'Cyrus Torrence (ankle), linebacker Dorian Williams (calf) and defensive lineman T.J. Sanders (shoulder) — all five limited in practice this week after Benford and Kincaid missed the Miami game entirely. The cleared list matters just as much: edge rusher Greg Rousseau (back), defensive tackle Ed Oliver (oblique), right tackle Spencer Brown (back) and safety Damar Hamlin (toe/neck) were full participants and carry no game designation, per the same official report. Buffalo's pass rush and its starting right tackle are whole. Its top corner and its leading receiver are coin flips until inactives post, about 90 minutes before kickoff.

Kansas City's report moved the number, too. The Chiefs ruled out running back Kenneth Walker III for the third straight game with a groin injury, the team announced Wednesday, per Reuters. Rookie Emmett Johnson receives his third consecutive start — and he has not played like a backup: Johnson has averaged 103.0 rushing yards and totaled three touchdowns (one rushing, two receiving) in Walker's absence, per Reuters. Kansas City also ruled out right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) and defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (knee), and listed tight end Noah Gray (ribs) and defensive tackle Peter Woods (neck) as questionable after both practiced fully, per the Chiefs' final report via the Bills' official site. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes (knee/right elbow), wide receiver Rashee Rice (knee) and right guard Trey Smith (concussion) carry no designation and will play, per the same report.

The matchup underneath the prices is a streak fight. Buffalo's defense has gone 43 consecutive opponent drives and 15 consecutive quarters without allowing a touchdown, per the Democrat and Chronicle — built, as this site's Film Room graded honestly on Tuesday, against a run of backup quarterbacks. Mahomes arrives with 13 touchdown passes and no interceptions across his last four games, per NFL on CBS via Bills Wire. Something breaks tonight. On the ground, Kansas City's run defense ranks 10th in the league at 95.5 yards allowed per game, per the Democrat and Chronicle — but it has not faced James Cook, who needs 75 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown tonight to tie Terry Allen's all-time record of 10 straight games hitting both marks, per Buffalo Rumblings. Cook behind a cleared Spencer Brown, against a Chiefs interior missing Norman-Lott and sweating Woods, is Buffalo's cleanest path to controlling this game — and shortening it.

Then there is the third opponent, and it is the other reason the total fell five points. Tonight's forecast calls for rain, temperatures in the mid-30s and wind gusts up to 24 mph at Highmark Stadium, per Covers' game-day update, and earlier National Weather Service discussion via the Democrat and Chronicle put possible gusts at 35 to 40 mph with 1 to 2 inches of rain across western New York. Rain and wind do not stop Mahomes or Josh Allen. They do slick the football, shorten throws, punish ball security and reward the team that can hand off 30 times and hold on. That team, on paper, is Buffalo — second in the NFL at 31.3 points per game, per the Democrat and Chronicle, but built this month on Cook and a defense that does not allow touchdowns.

Here is my card for tonight, in order. One: Buffalo to win is the lean, but at 58 percent on Kalshi and -151 at the books there is no bargain in it — the market already believes, so I am not paying full price to agree with it. Two: the spread at Buffalo -3 is a small lean toward the home team, and it is entirely an inactives bet. Rousseau, Oliver and Brown being cleared is real; if Benford and Kincaid are both active, -3 at home in the rain is a fair price for the AFC's top seed. If both sit, I pass — a rookie-corner secondary against Mahomes is not a 3-point favorite I want. Three: the total is a discipline test. Under 50.5 was the play on Monday; at 45.5, per NBC Sports, that value is gone, and chasing a number five points late is how this desk loses money. The only total I would touch is the under at Kalshi's 47.5, per Covers — two full points above the book number, in the rain, with a Buffalo team that wants this game played in the mud. Trade the inactives, not the rumors.

Tonight's inactives, about 90 minutes before the 8:20 PM ET kickoff, are the last word on Benford, Kincaid, Torrence, Williams, Sanders, Gray and Woods — everything above is priced to change when they post. body: Fourteen names opened the week on Buffalo's injury report, and on Monday the list read like a problem: cornerback Christian Benford was the lone Bill listed as a non-participant on an estimated report, per Bills On SI. Twenty-four hours later, the same list reads like a rally. The Buffalo Bills held a walkthrough on Tuesday, and all 14 injured players participated in some capacity, per Bills On SI. Head coach Joe Brady put it this way, per the same reporting: "I know it's walkthrough today, but everybody will be out there today. We'll kind of just continue to evaluate it through Thursday. Obviously, not practicing today, but everybody seems like they're in as good of a place as we can be right now." A walkthrough is not a full practice, and nobody in Orchard Park is treating it like one — the final game designations are due Wednesday, and they are the last official word before the Kansas City Chiefs (8-2) visit on Thanksgiving night, Thursday, Nov. 26 at 8:20 PM ET at Highmark Stadium on NBC. But on a four-day week, Tuesday was the best injury news Buffalo could have gotten.

The headline name is Benford. The starting cornerback was upgraded to a limited participant on Tuesday after being estimated as a non-participant on Monday, per Arrowhead Pride's Tuesday injury report. It is his first practice work of any kind since he injured his groin in the second half against the New York Jets on Nov. 15 — he did not practice at all last week and was ruled out Friday for the Miami game, per Bills On SI. The caution is real and it is on the record: Bills On SI noted it seems overly optimistic to expect Benford to fully recover from a groin issue in 11 days, and the team is taking a day-by-day approach. Limited on Tuesday is not cleared for Thursday. But a defense that started rookie Davison Igbinosun, Maxwell Hairston and a practice-squad elevation of Tre'Davious White against Miami just watched its top corner take the first step back — two days before Patrick Mahomes arrives with 13 touchdown passes and no interceptions across his last four games, per NFL on CBS via Bills Wire.

Tight end Dalton Kincaid is trending the same direction. Kincaid was a limited participant again Tuesday after being estimated as limited Monday, per Arrowhead Pride's report, in his first practice work since missing a game for the first time this season — he sat out the Miami win with thumb and ankle injuries after carrying a doubtful designation, per Bills On SI. Brady answered "yeah" last week when asked if Kincaid was close to being available against the Dolphins, per Bills On SI, and Kincaid himself thinks he will be ready to play Thursday night, per WGRZ's Jon Scott via Bills On SI. Linebacker Dorian Williams has been a limited participant all week after missing the Miami game with a calf injury, per Arrowhead Pride. Kincaid is Buffalo's leading receiver, and Williams was in the middle of a 61-tackle season before the Jets game ended his afternoon. Neither man is designated yet. Both men are moving toward the field instead of away from it, which is more than Buffalo could say on Friday.

The offensive line may have gotten the quietest good news of the day. Right tackle Spencer Brown was upgraded to a full participant Tuesday after being estimated as limited Monday with a back injury, per Arrowhead Pride, and Brown addressed reporters Tuesday without giving any reason to think he will not be available, per Bills On SI. Right guard O'Cyrus Torrence (ankle) remained limited — he popped up on Monday's report one day after playing 99 percent of the offensive snaps against Miami, per Bills On SI — and edge rusher Greg Rousseau, a new name Monday with a back issue, was limited while entertaining a media scrum after Tuesday's walkthrough and did not appear in any abnormal discomfort, per Bills On SI. On a night when the forecast is calling for Buffalo to run the football and protect it, a starting right side trending toward full strength is not a footnote. It is the game plan's foundation.

Kansas City's report moved, too. Running back Kenneth Walker III practiced on a limited basis Tuesday for the first time since his groin injury, per Arrowhead Pride — he has missed two straight games, and backup Emmett Johnson has exceeded 100 rushing yards and scored four touchdowns in his absence, per USA TODAY. Mahomes is on the Chiefs' report with knee and elbow issues but was listed as a full participant and is not expected to receive a game designation, per Heavy via SportsHub. And then there is the third opponent on the field Thursday: the weather. The National Weather Service expects a soaking rain to spread across western New York on Thursday with peak wind gusts of 35 to 40 mph possible Thursday afternoon and night, per the Democrat and Chronicle, a low near 35 with 1 to 2 inches of rain possible, per SportsHub, and AccuWeather RealFeel temperatures in the 20s throughout the game, per the Democrat and Chronicle. A snow game is not expected — this is a rain-and-wind game, the kind that shortens throws, tests ball security and rewards the team that can hand off and hold on.

The stage does not need inflating. Thursday is the first Thanksgiving home game in Bills history and the first holiday game at the new Highmark Stadium, per USA TODAY. Buffalo (9-1) holds the AFC's top spot, Kansas City (8-2) sits a game back, and according to the New York Times Playoff Predictor cited by the Bills' official site, Buffalo's chance at the No. 1 seed sits at 42 percent today — a win Thursday lifts it to 57 percent, a loss drops it to 20 percent. The football test inside the stakes is specific: Buffalo's offense went 2-for-5 in the red zone against Miami and settled for field goals, per the Bills' official site, and now faces Kansas City's top-ranked red zone defense, which has surrendered touchdowns on just 36 percent of red-zone trips this season, per the same preview. Wednesday's final report will give Benford, Kincaid, Williams, Torrence and Rousseau their official designations, and Thursday's inactives, about 90 minutes before kickoff, will settle what is left. Tuesday said everybody is coming. Wednesday decides who actually dresses. Go Bills — and get the final Chiefs designations and every Thanksgiving update in your inbox with The BNC Blitz.

body: Here is the number Buffalo's whole month is built on: 43 consecutive opponent drives without allowing a touchdown, a franchise record, and 15 consecutive quarters without an end-zone trip, per the Democrat and Chronicle. Here is the number standing across from it on Thanksgiving night: Patrick Mahomes has thrown 13 touchdown passes without an interception across his past four games, per NFL on CBS via Bills Wire, and eight of those touchdowns have come in the last two weeks, per Sports Illustrated. When the Kansas City Chiefs (8-2) visit the Buffalo Bills (9-1) on Thursday, Nov. 26 at 8:20 PM ET at Highmark Stadium on NBC — the first Thanksgiving home game in Bills history, per the Democrat and Chronicle — one of those streaks is the truth about a Super Bowl defense. The other one is a schedule artifact. Film Room has watched every snap of the streak. This is the week we find out which is which.

Start by grading the streak honestly, because the quarterbacks are part of the film. Buffalo's touchdown-less run has been built against a revolving door: undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano in relief for Baltimore, Carson Wentz and Max Brosmer for Minnesota, rookie Cade Klubnik in relief for the Jets, and Kyle McCord making his second career start for Miami — the sixth backup quarterback Buffalo has faced in four games, per the Democrat and Chronicle's reporting earlier this month. Those five quarterbacks combined for a 48.1 percent completion rate, zero touchdowns and four interceptions in that stretch, per the same reporting. Defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard's unit deserves real credit — you can only bury the quarterback in front of you, and Buffalo has buried all of them — but nobody in Orchard Park is pretending McCord-to-Mahomes is a small step up. Second-year defensive tackle Deone Walker said it plainly, per Bills Wire: "It's a big test. But coach Brady, the whole year keeps saying put the ball down. Nameless, faceless opponents, put the ball down, no matter what."

Now grade Mahomes' heater the same way. Kansas City has won three straight by at least 20 points — something the Chiefs had not done since 1997, per the Democrat and Chronicle — but those wins came against the Jets, Falcons and Cardinals. Mahomes' season line is 22 touchdown passes against just four interceptions with more than 2,700 passing yards, per Sports Illustrated, and he is not hiding his confidence. "I'm playing good football," Mahomes told CBS Sports' Evan Washburn, per Bills Wire. "I think it helps when you run the football like we're running it, and the receivers and tight ends making plays for me. But we gotta keep it going." The film question for Leonhard is pressure: Greg Rousseau just posted the first double-digit sack season of his career with two sacks against Miami, per Sports Illustrated — but Rousseau was also a new name on Monday's injury report, limited with a back issue on an estimated report from a walkthrough day, per Bills On SI. Buffalo's streak has been built on heat without blitzing itself into trouble. If the heat does not travel, Mahomes will hold the ball, extend plays and test the exact part of this defense that has not been tested in a month.

That part is the secondary, and Monday's report — estimated participations only, because Buffalo did not hold an official practice, per Bills On SI — kept the biggest question of the week open. Cornerback Christian Benford (groin) was the lone Bill listed as a non-participant, and Bills On SI noted it seems overly optimistic to expect him back 11 days after the injury, with another practice-squad call-up for Tre'Davious White looking likely. White played 42 percent of the defensive snaps against Miami in his first live action of the season, per Bills On SI, alongside rookie Davison Igbinosun and Maxwell Hairston. Against McCord, that group allowed 102 passing yards. Against Mahomes, the margin for a single busted coverage is a touchdown that ends a 43-drive streak on one play. The good news on the same report: defensive tackle Ed Oliver (oblique) was a full participant, and tight end Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle) and linebacker Dorian Williams (calf) were both limited after missing the Miami game — head coach Joe Brady answered "yeah" when asked if Kincaid was close to being available this past Sunday, per Bills On SI.

The counterpunch is on the ground, and it might be the most important matchup of the night. Kansas City's run defense ranks 10th in the league at 95.5 yards allowed per game and has held five teams to 77 yards or less, per the Democrat and Chronicle — but it has not faced James Cook, who ranks third in the NFL at 106 rushing yards per game, per the same preview. Cook also walks in with history on the line: his 89 yards and a touchdown against Miami made him the first player in NFL history with at least 75 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown in nine straight games in a single season, per the Bills, and one more such game ties Terry Allen's all-time record of 10 straight, set across the 1995 and 1996 seasons, per Buffalo Rumblings. Buffalo's offense ranks second in the NFL at 31.3 points per game, per the Democrat and Chronicle, but it is coming off its sloppiest outing of the year — two touchdowns on five red-zone trips, two Josh Allen interceptions and three sacks taken against a 1-9 Miami team. The cleanest way to protect a banged-up secondary from Mahomes is to keep him on the sideline, and the cleanest way to do that is Cook behind an offensive line that now has right tackle Spencer Brown (back) and right guard O'Cyrus Torrence (ankle) both limited on Monday's estimated report, per Bills On SI. Wide receiver DJ Moore, at least, is a full go in every way that matters: he does not appear on the injury report at all after hyperextending his knee against Miami, and Brady raved about him Monday, per Bills On SI: "Sometimes, I wish he wasn't as tough. He's kind of like Josh, when he gets tackled, I just hope he gets up, because of how important he is."

The stakes need no selling, but the tiebreaker math does. Buffalo and Kansas City have split their 10 meetings since 2020 at five apiece — Allen is 5-1 in the regular season, Mahomes is 4-0 in the playoffs, and three of those four playoff losses came at Arrowhead Stadium, per the Democrat and Chronicle. That is why Thursday is worth more than a game in the standings, where the 9-1 Bills sit atop the AFC with the 8-2 Chiefs and 8-2 Denver Broncos drafting behind them, per the same preview: win, and any January rematch runs through Orchard Park. Allen is keeping the framing small, per the Democrat and Chronicle: "It's the most important one because it's the next one. All the seeding implications, all that is what it is. We know what type of team they are, they've been one of the best teams in the league the last 10 years." Brady echoed it, per Bills Wire: "We only played one game this week, and it was this one. Now that this is over, now we'll regroup and figure out what we've got to do to go out on Thursday." Even the weather is joining the defense's side of the argument — the National Weather Service forecast discussion calls for steady, soaking rain moving in Thursday with temperatures in the upper 30s to low 40s and breezy conditions in Orchard Park, per the Democrat and Chronicle, with snow not expected to be the primary concern. Rain does not stop Mahomes. It does shorten games, slick the football and reward the team that can hand off 30 times.

So here is the Film Room verdict, and it is the same one this desk has been building toward for three weeks: the streak is real, and Thursday is its final exam. Buffalo's defense has not allowed a touchdown since Derrick Henry's 2-yard run on Nov. 1, per AP reporting earlier this month. It has done it with a rookie corner, a practice-squad All-Pro, a safety playing on a bad toe and a front that finally has its sack leader in double digits. Mahomes arrives with 13 touchdowns and no interceptions in four games, a three-game win streak by 20-plus, and a 4-0 playoff record against this franchise that hangs over every meeting until Buffalo changes it. If the streak survives Thanksgiving night, stop calling it a schedule artifact — it is the identity of the AFC's No. 1 seed. If it breaks in the first quarter, the 9-1 record still stands, but the January question gets louder. Either way, we stop guessing on Thursday. Go Bills — and get every Chiefs-week practice report, starting with Tuesday's update on Benford, Kincaid and Williams, in your inbox every morning with The BNC Blitz.

body: The Buffalo Bills are 9-1 for the first time since 1991, and they got there the hard way to watch. Buffalo beat the Miami Dolphins 26-9 on Sunday at Highmark Stadium — a sixth straight win and an 11th straight home win over Miami, per Reuters — behind 304 passing yards from Josh Allen and 89 rushing yards and a touchdown from James Cook, per Reuters. The scoreboard says comfortable. Nobody in the home locker room described it that way. Head coach Joe Brady, with no smile in sight, put it plainly, per the Democrat and Chronicle: "I enjoy winning. I enjoy it for the guys, but we've got to continue to get better." Allen called it a luxury to be 9-1 and still be, in his words via Athlon Sports, "a little ticked off" about the performance. Both things are true, and the next four days will decide which one matters more.

Start with the history, because Sunday made some. Cook carried 22 times for 89 yards and a one-yard touchdown, per the Bills' official recap — and with that, he became the first player in NFL history to rush for at least 75 yards and a touchdown in nine consecutive games in a single season, per the Bills. The streak passes LaDainian Tomlinson (eight straight in 2006) and John Riggins (eight straight in 1983), per the Bills, and Cook now sits one game behind Terry Allen's overall record of 10 straight, set across the 1995 and 1996 seasons, per Buffalo Rumblings. The touchdown was also a franchise first — nine straight games with a rushing score — and it pushed Cook past 1,000 rushing yards for the season, to 1,060, making him just the second Bill ever to reach 1,000 in the first 10 games of a season, joining O.J. Simpson in 1973 and 1975, per the Democrat and Chronicle. One more Cook note for the record book: he and Allen are now the first pair of teammates in NFL history with at least 10 rushing touchdowns in three consecutive seasons, per the Bills' official recap. Film Room told you Friday that Cook needed one normal Sunday. He delivered it, and the record book moved.

The defense, meanwhile, has stopped allowing touchdowns altogether. Miami managed 185 total yards and three field goals, per theScore's game summary and NBC Sports, which noted this is the third straight game Buffalo has allowed nothing more than a field goal. The streaks underneath that are staggering: 43 consecutive opponent drives without allowing a touchdown, a franchise record, per the Democrat and Chronicle, and 15 consecutive quarters without an end-zone trip, per the same reporting. Dolphins quarterback Kyle McCord, making his second career start, completed just 12 of 33 passes for 102 yards and threw an interception to Damar Hamlin, per the Democrat and Chronicle. Greg Rousseau recorded two sacks in the first half, his ninth and 10th of the season — the first double-digit sack season of his career, per Sports Illustrated. And Tre'Davious White, elevated from the practice squad with Christian Benford out, played 42 percent of the defensive snaps in his first live action of the season, per Bills On SI. Defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard's unit was the problem in September. In late November, it is the identity of a 9-1 team.

Now the part Allen is ticked off about, because it is real. Buffalo piled up 405 yards and 25 first downs, per the Democrat and Chronicle, but scored touchdowns on only two of five trips inside Miami's 20-yard line, per Athlon Sports, and settled for four Tyler Bass field goals, per the Democrat and Chronicle. Allen finished 27 of 45 for 304 yards and one touchdown with two interceptions, both in the first half, per Athlon Sports. The Democrat and Chronicle's report card graded the pass offense and run offense both at C, noting the offensive line could not create the gaps Buffalo is used to and Cook had to work for almost every one of his 89 yards. Against a banged-up Miami defense missing its interior, that is a fair grade — and it is exactly the kind of afternoon that gets a team beat on Thursday night.

The receivers carried the passing game while tight end Dalton Kincaid sat out. Khalil Shakir caught five passes for 101 yards, including gains of 38 and 32 — the sixth 100-yard game of his career, per the Democrat and Chronicle. DJ Moore caught eight passes for 91 yards and a touchdown, and five of his catches produced first downs, per the same reporting. Moore also gave Buffalo its newest short-week worry: he hyperextended his knee in the first half, left the field briefly, and returned to finish the game, per Athlon Sports. He said so himself after the game, per the same reporting. On a week with three days of preparation, Moore's knee is the first name to watch when practice reports post.

The strangest highlight belonged to the punter who never punted. Buffalo did not punt once all afternoon — and on its only punt formation, a fourth-and-8 from its own 34 in the first quarter, rookie Tommy Doman threw a 30-yard pass to tight end Keleki Latu on a fake, per Sports Illustrated. Doman is the first Bills punter to complete a pass since Chris Mohr in 2000, per the same reporting, and he added a tackle on a kickoff for good measure. It was that kind of day: a fake punt for 30, four field goals, two interceptions, a franchise-record defensive streak, an NFL record for the running back — and a 17-point win that still left the quarterback annoyed.

Which brings us to Thursday. The Kansas City Chiefs, 8-2 and fresh off a 34-7 win over Arizona, per the Democrat and Chronicle, visit Highmark Stadium on Thanksgiving night, Nov. 26. Buffalo's streak of 15 straight quarters without allowing a touchdown has been built against Fagnano, Wentz, Klubnik and McCord. Patrick Mahomes is none of those names, and everyone in Orchard Park knows it — Allen said it himself, per the Democrat and Chronicle: "We know what type of team they are." The Bills are 9-1, alone on top of the AFC East, with Cook chasing Terry Allen's record and a defense chasing a fourth straight game without allowing a touchdown. They also have three days to fix a red-zone offense that just went 2-for-5 against a 1-9 team. Enjoy 9-1 tonight. The real exam starts Thursday. Go Bills — and get every Chiefs-week practice report, starting with DJ Moore's knee, in your inbox every morning with The BNC Blitz.

body: Welcome back to The Card — I'm Matt Manzella, and this is the one desk on this site where we talk about the numbers that move money. This is Partner Content, presented by Kalshi, the regulated exchange where you trade on game outcomes instead of betting against a house. The rule here has not changed since this desk opened: every number below traces to a named source, every position gets logged in public, and there are no locks and no guarantees. Today's game is the Miami Dolphins (1-8) at the Buffalo Bills (8-1), Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 PM ET at Highmark Stadium on CBS — and the most honest price in this matchup is not the spread. It is the total, and it has been falling all week.

Start with the headline prices. The consensus spread has not moved: Buffalo -16.5, unchanged since tracking began Wednesday, per The Sharp Edition's Sunday-morning update, with Kalshi listing the same -16.5 spread, a 45 total and a Buffalo win price implying about a 91.5 percent chance on Sunday morning, per the same update. The sportsbook total sits at 44.5, per Action Network and BetMGM listings checked this morning — down from an open of 46.5, per The Sharp Edition, and some previews put the open as high as 47. A two-point fall in a total with no move in the spread is the market telling a specific story: it still believes Buffalo wins big, but it no longer believes this game gets played in a track meet. The forecast is part of it — wind at 14 miles per hour, gusting to 23, at Highmark Stadium, per The Sharp Edition's kickoff forecast, with the total dropping two points as that forecast firmed up.

Saturday then changed the defense that has to protect that margin. Buffalo elevated cornerback Tre'Davious White and linebacker Shaq Thompson from the practice squad on Saturday, per the Democrat and Chronicle — two former first-round picks called up because cornerback Christian Benford (groin) and linebacker Dorian Williams (calf) were ruled out Friday after missing all three practices, per the same reporting. Rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr is expected to make his first NFL start in place of Williams, and Buffalo could start rookie Davison Igbinosun and second-year corner Maxwell Hairston outside with Benford sidelined, per the Democrat and Chronicle. White and Thompson could see their first action of the season. That is real depth, and it is also real inexperience in the starting group in front of it — against a 1-8 team, that trade favors Buffalo. Against a 16.5-point spread, every communication mistake is a backdoor waiting to open.

Saturday added one more name, and it is the swing name on the whole card. Defensive tackle Ed Oliver was added to Buffalo's injury report on Saturday with an oblique injury and listed as questionable, per the Democrat and Chronicle — one day after he finished the practice week with no designation at all. Buffalo will announce its inactives about 90 minutes before kickoff, and Oliver's status is now the last word on this game. If he plays, Buffalo's interior faces a Miami line that may be without its starting center — Aaron Brewer is questionable as he finishes the concussion protocol, per the Dolphins' report via the Democrat and Chronicle — with its run game already thinned by De'Von Achane's season-ending injury. If Oliver sits, Miami's only real path, keeping quarterback Kyle McCord out of third-and-long behind running back Ollie Gordon II, gets a little wider. Tight end Dalton Kincaid (thumb and ankle) remains doubtful after missing all week, and safety Damar Hamlin, tight end Jackson Hawes and defensive tackle T.J. Sanders are questionable, per the Democrat and Chronicle's Sunday update; nickel corner Dee Alford cleared the concussion protocol, practiced fully Friday and carries no designation.

The matchup the price is built on is still the ground game, and the grades say it is not close. James Cook has 971 rushing yards at 5.2 yards per carry with nine touchdowns, per Athlon Sports, and he ran for 157 yards against the Jets last week while chasing a piece of history this site's Film Room detailed Friday: 75 rushing yards and a touchdown today would be his ninth straight game hitting both marks, alone in second place in NFL history. Miami's interior is gone — Zach Sieler lost for the season, and Zeek Biggers and Jordan Phillips placed on injured reserve this week, per the Democrat and Chronicle — and Indianapolis ran for 172 yards on the Dolphins last week before those moves, per Athlon. Buffalo averages 152.7 rushing yards per game, second in the league, per Athlon. The one Dolphin who can wreck a drive is edge rusher Chop Robinson: a 79.9 PFF pass-rush grade, eighth among 111 qualifiers, and a 19.9 percent pressure rate that leads all edge rushers, per TruMedia via Athlon — but his run-defense grade is 50.8, per the same reporting, and Buffalo is going to run at him. On the other side, Greg Rousseau has 53 pressures on 296 pass-rush snaps, per PFF via Athlon, and rookie T.J. Parker piled up five pressures on 26 pass-rush snaps against the Jets, per PFF via FanRecap — a lot of heat for a quarterback making his second career start.

So why is the total falling if Buffalo's offense is this good? Because the other prices are honest, too. Josh Allen carries an 82.3 PFF grade, seventh among 37 quarterbacks, per PFF — and he has also thrown an interception in each of his last three games, seven on the season, per ESPN via Athlon, with Miami rookie cornerback Chris Johnson, one of two Dolphins rookies in PFF's top 15, coming off a pick-six in Indianapolis, per Athlon. Buffalo's defense has not allowed a touchdown in 33 consecutive drives and has given up 28 points total across its last three games, per the Bills' official recap reporting this week. And hanging over all of it is the calendar: Kansas City arrives on Thanksgiving night, four days from now. A Buffalo team up three scores in the fourth quarter has every reason to hand the ball off, drain the clock and get Cook and Allen to Thursday healthy. That is how favorites win comfortably and totals stay under — and how 16.5-point spreads die by a late, meaningless Miami touchdown.

Here is my card for today, in order. One: Buffalo to win is the only moneyline lean, but at a price implying better than 90 percent on Kalshi there is no edge in chasing it — the market already believes, so I am not paying full price to agree with it. Two: the spread at -16.5 is a pass until inactives. If Oliver is active, the case for a comfortable cover is real; if he is out, with two rookie outside corners and a rookie starting at linebacker, 16.5 is a number I respect too much to lay. Three: the total is my lean — under 44.5 at the books, around the 45 line on Kalshi — on the wind, on a falling market, on a defense riding a 33-drive touchdown-less streak, and on a short-week incentive to shorten this game the moment it is in hand. The expert score predictions collected by the Palm Beach Post — Buffalo 28-13, 30-15 and 31-19 — all land in that same neighborhood: a clear Buffalo win that does not need a shootout to happen. Trade the inactives, not the rumors.

body: The reports are over. The rulings are in. Head coach Joe Brady announced on Friday that cornerback Christian Benford and linebacker Dorian Williams have been ruled out for Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins, per Pro Football Talk, and tight end Dalton Kincaid is listed as doubtful with thumb and ankle injuries after not practicing all week, per the Bills' final injury report via Yardbarker. When the Miami Dolphins (1-8) visit the Buffalo Bills (8-1) on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 PM ET at Highmark Stadium, Buffalo will play a division game without its top cornerback, without a starting linebacker, and in all likelihood without its leading receiver. The good news arrived on the same report: nickel cornerback Dee Alford practiced fully on Friday, carries no injury designation, and cleared the concussion protocol, per Miami Dolphins on SI. Friday did not just shrink Buffalo's roster. It redrew Sunday's defense.

Benford's absence is the headline, and the timeline is the concern. He sustained the groin injury in the fourth quarter of Sunday's 31-12 win at the Jets, did not practice at all this week, and finishes the week ruled out, per Pro Football Talk. His season line is the size of the hole: 33 tackles and eight passes defensed in eight starts, per Pro Football Talk. There is a ceiling on the worry, at least. Brady said neither Benford's nor Williams' injury is seen as long term, per Heavy's reporting of Bills reporter Chris Brown, and the hope is that Benford will be available on Thanksgiving night against the Kansas City Chiefs, per the same reporting. That is a hope, not a designation — but it frames Sunday correctly. This is a one-week problem Buffalo has to solve, not a season problem it has to survive.

Brady already told us the first part of the solution. The head coach said Alford can slide outside from the nickel to replace Benford, with Jordan Hancock moving into the slot, per Yardbarker. Alford earned that trust the hard way this week: evaluated for a concussion twice against the Jets, cleared once, ruled out, then through the protocol and a full participant by Friday with no designation, per Miami Dolphins on SI. Behind that plan, Maxwell Hairston will presumably start opposite rookie Davison Igbinosun, per Sports Illustrated — and here is the roster math that makes Saturday worth watching: Buffalo has no other true outside cornerback on the 53-man roster behind those starters, per Sports Illustrated, so for numbers alone the Bills likely need a game-day addition. The most practical move is a practice-squad elevation of Tre'Davious White or undrafted rookie Kani Walker, per the same reporting, with any elevation due by Saturday's deadline. Brady is not tipping it: "If we have to have any practice squad call-ups, we feel comfortable with the guys on there," he said after Friday's practice, per Sports Illustrated. This desk wrote Wednesday that Buffalo brought White back on Oct. 19 for exactly this week. Friday made the week official. Saturday tells us if the call comes.

Williams is the quieter loss, and the numbers say it should not be. He appeared in all nine games this season with 61 tackles, two interceptions, a sack and a fumble recovery, per Pro Football Talk — and his last full game was his loudest, a team-high nine tackles with two quarterback hits and his first career sack against the Jets before the calf injury ended his afternoon, per the Democrat and Chronicle's reporting earlier this week. Rookie Kaleb Elarms-Orr will get most of the work at linebacker with Williams out, per Yardbarker. Elarms-Orr already owns a piece of this defense's streak — he recovered the fumble on the Jets' backfired hook-and-lateral last Sunday — and now a defense that has gone 33 consecutive drives without allowing a touchdown hands a rookie a starting share of the middle against a Dolphins offense with nothing left to lose.

On offense, doubtful is the word doing the damage. Kincaid leads the Bills with 487 receiving yards, and his 32 catches rank second on the team, per Yardbarker — and a doubtful tag after a full week of missed practice almost always means watching in street clothes. Dawson Knox, who has 14 receptions, would be the top option, per the same reporting, but the depth behind him is the real squeeze: Jackson Hawes is questionable after being limited all week with a shoulder injury, and Hawes and Keleki Latu have three catches between them, per Yardbarker. That matters beyond the passing game, because Buffalo uses a three-tight-end package on 29 percent of its offensive plays, the second-highest rate in the league, per the same reporting. Lose Kincaid, sweat Hawes, and an entire personnel family shrinks. The counterweight is the one this site's Film Room wrote about yesterday: James Cook, who needs 75 rushing yards and a touchdown to stand alone in second place in NFL history with nine straight games hitting both marks. A thinner tight end room is one more reason Sunday's plan runs through No. 4.

The rest of Friday's list is shorter, and Miami's is its own kind of mess. Buffalo also listed safety Damar Hamlin (toe) and defensive lineman T.J. Sanders (shoulder) as questionable, per the final report via Yardbarker. Miami ruled out punter Bradley Pinion and wide receiver Jared Wayne, listed starting safety Dante Trader Jr. and cornerback Jaylin Simpson as doubtful, and listed center Aaron Brewer, cornerback Darrell Baker Jr. and cornerback Marcellas Dial Jr. as questionable, per the Dolphins' official report. Brewer took the final step out of the concussion protocol with a full practice Friday and is trending toward playing, per Miami Dolphins on SI, while Miami's Saturday moves are expected to sort out a new punter in Jack Browning and a new kicker in Daniel Carlson, per the same reporting — a 1-8 team changing both specialists and starting a quarterback in his second career start, walking into the loudest building in the division.

So Sunday's checklist is set, and only one document can still change it: the inactives, about 90 minutes before the 1 PM ET kickoff, which will give the final word on Kincaid, Hamlin, Sanders and Hawes. Everything else is decided. Buffalo is 8-1, chasing a 9-1 start and a sixth straight win, with Kansas City arriving four days later on Thanksgiving night — which is exactly why Friday's rulings, frustrating as they are, may be the right kind of conservative. Benford and Williams get the extra days. The rookies get a 1-8 opponent at home instead of Patrick Mahomes on a short week. And a defense that has not allowed a touchdown in 33 drives gets one more test of the only thing that has defined it all month: the next man up actually being ready. Go Bills — and get every inactives update and Dolphins fallout in your inbox with The BNC Blitz.

body: James Cook does not need a career day on Sunday to make NFL history. He needs a normal one. When the Miami Dolphins (1-8) visit the Buffalo Bills (8-1) on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 PM ET at Highmark Stadium, Cook needs 75 rushing yards and one rushing touchdown — his season averages are 107.9 yards a game — to do something no running back has done in 20 years. Cook has hit both marks in eight straight games, a streak the Bills' official site notes ties John Riggins in 1983 and LaDainian Tomlinson in 2006, with George Rogers (1985-86) also at eight, per the Democrat and Chronicle's record list. One more Sunday and Cook stands alone in second place in NFL history, one game behind Terry Allen's record of 10 straight (1995-96), per Buffalo Rumblings. Film Room has spent three weeks writing about Buffalo's defense. This week, the most important film in Orchard Park is a running back who keeps turning ordinary Sundays into record-book problems.

Start with the Jets tape, because it shows why this streak is not a stat-padding accident. Cook led the NFL in Week 10 with 157 rushing yards and a touchdown, per the Bills' official advanced-stats breakdown, and the touchdown was a 74-yard sprint down the right sideline — the longest run of his career and the second-longest rush in the league this year. Next Gen Stats had him at 21.56 miles per hour on the play, his fastest top speed of the season, per the same breakdown. The expected-yards model gave that outside zone run 10 yards; Cook took 74, good for plus-64 rushing yards over expected on a single carry and plus-75 for the game — the highest total of any rusher in Week 10 — which pushed his season total to plus-167, fourth-most in the NFL, per the Bills. He averaged 8.7 yards a carry, added a plus-5.2 rushing EPA (second-highest in Week 10) and created an extra 4.1 yards per carry over expected, per the same breakdown. That is not a back falling forward into a streak. That is a back breaking the model's math once a week.

The streak is also built in the trenches, and the Jets game is the clearest picture of it yet. Buffalo led the league in Week 10 with 4.09 rushing yards before contact per attempt, per the Bills' breakdown — Cook was getting into clean space before a defender touched him — and the Bills were stopped for no gain or a loss on just 3.1 percent of rushes, the NFL's second-lowest run-stuffed rate that week. New York knew what was coming and loaded up anyway: Buffalo faced a stacked box of eight or more defenders on 46.9 percent of plays, the second-highest rate in the league, and still ran the ball on 59.3 percent of its snaps, the fifth-highest run rate of the week, per the Bills. For the season, Cook sits at 971 rushing yards on 187 carries — 5.2 yards per carry and 107.9 per game — with nine rushing touchdowns, per Athlon Sports' Week 11 breakdown, and his rushing touchdown against the Jets also tied the Bills' franchise record with his eighth consecutive game with a rushing touchdown, per the Bills' official recap. Defenses are selling out to stop a streak, and the streak is eating the extra defender for lunch.

Now look at what is waiting for him in the middle of Miami's defense, because this is where Sunday's matchup stops being fair. The Colts just ran for 172 yards on the Dolphins last week with Jonathan Taylor and Seth McGowan, per Athlon Sports — and that was before Miami's interior fell apart. The Dolphins placed defensive linemen Zeek Biggers and Jordan Phillips on injured reserve on Tuesday after both were hurt in that 24-22 loss to Indianapolis, per the Democrat and Chronicle, and defensive tackle Zach Sieler was already lost for the season — three interior defensive linemen gone from a defense that now has to hold the middle with Kenneth Grant and a practice-squad call-up against the NFL's second-ranked rushing offense, per Athlon. Buffalo averages 152.67 rushing yards per game, second in the league, and leads the NFL in rushing touchdowns at 2.22 per game, per NBC Sports' preview. Film Room will keep the receipt, though: Miami still ranks sixth in EPA per run allowed, per Sports Illustrated via Athlon, and linebacker Jordyn Brooks leads the Dolphins with 84 tackles, per Athlon. The Dolphins' run fits have been better than their record. The question Sunday is whether a gutted tackle rotation can keep those fits intact for four quarters against the league's hottest back.

Cook's workload may grow for a second reason, and it is sitting on Thursday's practice report. Tight end Dalton Kincaid — Buffalo's leading receiver — missed practice for the second straight day Thursday with thumb and ankle injuries, per the Democrat and Chronicle, and backup running back Ray Davis remained limited with a hamstring injury, per the same report; cornerback Christian Benford (groin), linebacker Dorian Williams (calf) and safety Damar Hamlin (toe) also missed Thursday, with Friday's final designations and Sunday's inactives still to come. If Kincaid cannot go, the middle-of-the-field passing game that stretches defenses away from the box shrinks with him — and the answer, all season, has been Cook: more carries, more screens, more of the offense running through No. 4. Head coach Joe Brady is not entertaining trap-game talk either way. "I think it's always been disrespectful to the players and the profession when people think one game is less important or going to be easier," Brady said Wednesday, per Athlon Sports via the Bills' official site.

There is a team record riding shotgun here, too. A win Sunday gives Buffalo its first 9-1 start since 1991, per Buffalo Rumblings, and keeps the Bills on top of the AFC with the Bengals, Jaguars and Chiefs all sitting at 7-2 behind them, per the Democrat and Chronicle. The ideal script writes itself: lean on Cook early, let him chase 75 and a score behind a line that just produced the league's best yards-before-contact week, build the lead, and get him rest in the fourth quarter with Kansas City arriving on Thanksgiving night — four days later. That is not looking past Miami. That is what a run game this good is for in late November: it shortens games, protects a banged-up roster and travels into January.

So here is the Film Room watch list for Sunday. The yards should come at Cook's pace — at 107.9 a game, the 75-yard line is a third-quarter question, not a fourth-quarter sweat. The touchdown is the swing play, the one that turns a strong afternoon into sole possession of second place, past Riggins, Rogers and Tomlinson, with Terry Allen's 10 straight suddenly live on Thanksgiving night against the Chiefs. Twenty years since Tomlinson did it. Eight straight Sundays and counting. One normal James Cook game is all that stands between Buffalo and a little more room in the record book. Go Bills — and get every Dolphins fallout and record update in your inbox Monday morning with The BNC Blitz.

body: Tyrell Shavers is back on the Buffalo Bills' roster, and the date on the calendar is the whole story. The Bills activated Shavers from the physically unable to perform list on Wednesday, per the Democrat and Chronicle, clearing the way for his season debut when the Miami Dolphins (1-8) visit Highmark Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 PM ET. He tore his ACL in the playoffs on Jan. 11. He returned to practice on Oct. 28 — 290 days after suffering the injury, per the same reporting. Activation does not guarantee he suits up Sunday, per the Democrat and Chronicle. But after 290 days, the door is open, and the receiver Josh Allen calls one of his best teammates is standing in it.

To understand what 290 days cost him, you have to go back to the night it happened. Shavers tore his ACL on a special teams play — a punt return — in the second quarter of Buffalo's 27-24 wild-card victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars on Jan. 11, per the Democrat and Chronicle. Then he did the thing that still defines him in that building: he came back out for the second half and played 21 more snaps on offense, on the torn ACL, per ESPN's reporting. The Bills placed him on injured reserve three days later, ending his season. Most players would have been done for the night the moment the knee gave out. Shavers played a half of playoff football on it first.

The rehab that followed was a routine so fixed that general manager Brandon Beane could practically set his watch to it, per the Democrat and Chronicle: every morning around 6 a.m., Shavers was at the team's facility, preparing a saltwater bath, working his way back from the torn ACL. That is the unglamorous version of a comeback — no cameras, no countdown posts, just a 6 a.m. saltwater bath and ten months of mornings. He opened his 21-day practice window on Oct. 28, was a full participant for the past two weeks, per Rotowire, and the Bills had until Wednesday to add him to the 53-man roster or leave him on the PUP list for the rest of the season, per the Democrat and Chronicle. Tuesday, Buffalo placed rookie guard Ar'maj Reed-Adams on injured reserve, opening the roster spot. Wednesday, head coach Joe Brady announced Shavers was being activated, per Buffalo Rumblings. The deadline met the routine, right on time.

Shavers earned this return the slow way, and Buffalo fans who watched last season know the shape of it. He signed with the Bills as an undrafted free agent out of San Diego State in 2023 and spent his first two seasons primarily on the practice squad, per the Democrat and Chronicle. His first career catch was a 69-yard touchdown off a screen pass from Mitchell Trubisky in Week 17 of 2024 against the Jets. Last season he finally cracked the initial 53-man roster, appeared in all 17 regular-season games with nine starts, and finished with 15 receptions for 245 yards and one touchdown, per the Democrat and Chronicle — including his breakout against Tampa Bay in Week 11, four catches for 90 yards and a touchdown on a 43-yard pass from Josh Allen, per his career log. At 6-foot-4, he is the big-bodied receiver in a room built on quickness, and he contributes on special teams, where the injury found him. Nothing about his path was handed to him. The roster spot, the snaps, the breakout — all of it was earned in the margins.

What he walks back into is a receiver room that could use exactly what he brings, and a week that made that clearer. Wide receivers DJ Moore, Khalil Shakir and Keon Coleman sit ahead of him, per Rotowire, so Shavers figures to start as a depth option — but depth is doing real work in Buffalo right now. Tight end Dalton Kincaid, the team's leading receiver with 32 receptions for 497 yards and two touchdowns, per Heavy, did not practice Wednesday with a thumb injury on top of the ankle injury that limited him last week, per Pro Football Talk via Heavy — the thumb was picked up while catching two passes for 58 yards in Sunday's win over the Jets. Kincaid has appeared in all nine games this year, per Heavy, but Wednesday was a walkthrough estimate, not a ruling, and the Bills will not know what they have at tight end until the week's later reports. A 6-foot-4 receiver who blocks, plays special teams and already has Allen's trust is not a luxury in a week like that. It is insurance that can catch the ball.

The rest of Wednesday's report is the other half of Dolphins week, and it is the part this desk covered yesterday: cornerback Christian Benford (groin) and nickel cornerback Dee Alford (concussion) did not practice, per Pro Football Talk via Heavy, with safeties Cole Bishop (shoulder), Damar Hamlin (toe) and Amani Hooker (knee) limited, and linebacker Dorian Williams (calf) and right guard O'Cyrus Torrence (personal) also out. That is why the Tre'Davious White door stayed open in yesterday's column, and it stays open today. But Shavers is the other direction of the same week — the roster move that adds a player instead of subtracting one, on a Wednesday that mostly took them away.

Sunday will tell us how much of a role he gets, and this desk will not print a debut before the inactives do — about 90 minutes before the 1 PM ET kickoff. If he is in uniform, it will be against a 1-8 Dolphins team starting a quarterback making his second career start, in a game the 8-1 Bills are expected to control, which is as gentle a re-entry as the NFL ever offers. And if the moment is small — a few snaps, a block that springs a run, a special-teams rep — it will still be the end of 290 days that started with a torn ACL in a playoff game he refused to leave. He played the second half on it. He spent ten months earning his way back to the first half of the next one. Go Bills — and get every Dolphins-week practice report and roster move in your inbox every morning with The BNC Blitz.

body: The loudest moment at Highmark Stadium on Sunday might belong to a player who is not on the active roster yet. When the Miami Dolphins (1-8) visit the Buffalo Bills (8-1) on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 PM ET, Buffalo will be chasing a sixth straight win — and, if its injured defensive backs cannot go, Tre'Davious White could be back in a Buffalo Bills uniform, per reporting this morning from WBUF. White signed to Buffalo's practice squad last month, on Oct. 19, and he has not played a snap since. No elevation has been announced, and this desk is not printing one. But the door that was closed when he signed is open now, and everybody in Orchard Park knows why.

Start with the toll Sunday's 31-12 win at the Jets took on the secondary that built Buffalo's 33-drive touchdown-less streak. Cornerback Christian Benford was ruled out with a groin injury in the fourth quarter, per the Democrat and Chronicle. Nickel cornerback Dee Alford was evaluated for a concussion twice, was cleared to return once, then was ruled out, and must clear the NFL's concussion protocol before he can play against Miami, per the same reporting. Cornerback Maxwell Hairston was shaken up late, and linebacker Dorian Williams left with a calf injury, per the Democrat and Chronicle. That is the context Wednesday's first practice report of Dolphins week lands in — it is the first real clue about who is actually available, and until it posts, every one of those names is a report, not a ruling. If the rulings go the wrong way, Buffalo's next man up is not a rookie. It is No. 27.

The coaching staff has been quietly preparing for exactly this possibility. Defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard said he believes White is close to being ready to help the team, should he be called on, per Jay Skurski of The Buffalo News, via Buffalowdown. That word — ready — has been the whole project since Oct. 19. White joined in the middle of the season, into a new scheme under Leonhard, and it was always going to take time before he was up to speed, per Buffalowdown. He addressed the media on Oct. 28 about his return, his role, mentoring the next crop of defensive backs and what he was doing before Buffalo called, per the Bills' official site. A month of practice-squad work, learning a new defense in the building he used to own a corner of. That is not a nostalgia signing. That is an insurance policy being paid up, week by week, in case November ever looked like this. November looks like this.

To understand why Sunday would hit different, you have to remember who White was here. Buffalo drafted him in the first round, 27th overall, in 2017, and he started as a rookie on the team that ended the 17-year playoff drought — the Bills' first postseason appearance since 1999. By 2019 he was a first-team All-Pro, a Pro Bowler, and the NFL's co-leader in interceptions with six, in a season when he did not allow a single touchdown reception. For a fanbase that had spent two decades watching other teams' stars, White was proof the new era had a face on defense: homegrown, drafted, and shutting down his side of the field every Sunday. Buffalo did not just love Tre'Davious White. Buffalo believed in what he represented.

Which is why the middle of his story still stings. White tore his ACL on Thanksgiving night in 2021, in a game at New Orleans, in his home state of Louisiana, per ESPN's reporting on his recovery. Three injury-riddled seasons followed, then a release, then 2024 stops with the Los Angeles Rams and the Baltimore Ravens, then a return to Buffalo in 2025 — and this fall, a third stint, beginning on the practice squad in October. Most former All-Pros do not take that job. White took it in the city that drafted him, in a new scheme, with no promise attached. The No. 27 jerseys never actually left the Highmark Stadium stands while he was gone. On Sunday, one of them might jog out of the tunnel with a player inside it again.

The roster mechanics around him are moving, too. On Tuesday, Buffalo re-signed defensive back Te'Cory Couch to the practice squad just three days after releasing him, released guard Nick Broeker and placed guard Ar'maj Reed-Adams on injured reserve, per the Democrat and Chronicle — moves that leave the Bills with one open spot on the 53-man roster. Wide receiver Tyrell Shavers faces his own Wednesday deadline today to be activated from the reserve/PUP list, per the same reporting; that is a separate decision from White's, whose path to Sunday would run through a standard practice-squad elevation later in the week, after the practice reports sort out Benford and Alford. This secondary has already been remade once this month — safety Amani Hooker, acquired at the trade deadline, played all 71 defensive snaps in his debut against the Jets, per AP. White stepping in would be the second remake in three weeks, and the first one Buffalo planned back in October.

None of this guarantees a storybook Sunday. An elevation, if it comes, might mean a handful of snaps. It might mean emergency depth that never leaves the sideline. Benford and Alford might heal up and close the door again, and White's debut might wait for Kansas City on Thanksgiving night or beyond. But say it does happen: a 1-8 Dolphins team, a backup quarterback making his second career start, and Tre'Davious White — the drought-breaker, the All-Pro, the practice-squad cornerback who bet on himself in the only city that ever felt like his — running back onto the Highmark Stadium field in a Bills uniform, in a game that counts, for a defense that has not allowed a touchdown in 33 drives. Buffalo brought him back on Oct. 19 for a week exactly like this one. Sunday, we find out if the week has arrived. Go Bills — and get every Dolphins-week practice report and roster move in your inbox every morning with The BNC Blitz.

body: Kyle McCord is next. When the Miami Dolphins (1-8) visit the Buffalo Bills (8-1) on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 PM ET at Highmark Stadium, McCord will be the sixth backup quarterback Buffalo has faced in four games, per the Democrat and Chronicle, and Sunday will be just his second career NFL start. It will also mark the third straight week the Bills have faced a quarterback who had never thrown an NFL regular-season pass before November, per the same reporting. Buffalo has won five straight. The quarterbacks standing across from it keep changing mid-game anyway.

The revolving door started on Nov. 1, when Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson injured his throwing thumb on the first offensive snap, per the Democrat and Chronicle. Backup Tyler Huntley suffered a toe injury in the second quarter, which thrust undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano into his first NFL game. The following week, Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray missed the game with a hamstring injury; Carson Wentz started, posted an 8.9 passer rating and was replaced by Max Brosmer in the fourth quarter, per the same reporting. On Sunday against the Jets, Geno Smith exited twice — first to be evaluated for a concussion, then with an ankle injury — and fourth-round rookie Cade Klubnik made his NFL debut in relief. Three weeks, three starters gone, five backups already through the door. McCord makes six.

The five who came before him produced a combined line that explains Buffalo's month: a 48.1 percent completion rate, 367 passing yards, zero touchdowns, four interceptions and a 41.4 passer rating, per the Democrat and Chronicle, while Buffalo outscored its opponents 90-28 in that stretch. The Associated Press put the defensive run in clock terms: Buffalo has not allowed a touchdown since Derrick Henry's 2-yard run for Baltimore on Nov. 1 — a span of 168 minutes, 18 seconds — and has not trailed in 217 minutes, 13 seconds, dating to the second quarter of the Oct. 18 win at Las Vegas. A defense that averaged 28.5 points allowed through its first six games has given up a combined 28 points in its past three, per AP, and after forcing six turnovers in the first six games, it has forced eight in the past three. Defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard's unit is not just surviving backup quarterbacks. It is burying them.

McCord, though, is not arriving as a punchline, and his first start is the reason why. He set a franchise record in his NFL debut on Sunday, completing 17 of 32 passes for 209 yards — the most passing yards by a Dolphins quarterback in his debut — in Miami's 24-22 loss to Indianapolis, per the Democrat and Chronicle. He did not throw a touchdown or an interception, ran for a touchdown, and lost a fumble in his own end zone that Indianapolis recovered for a touchdown, per the same reporting, while Miami nearly erased a 21-7 second-half deficit. Dolphins head coach Jeff Hafley was encouraged by his demeanor, per the Democrat and Chronicle: "He was composed, he didn't get rattled." The college resume backs up the calm: McCord, 24, led the nation with 4,779 passing yards at Syracuse in 2024, an ACC single-season record, with 34 touchdown passes for a 10-3 team, per the same reporting. Drafted in the sixth round by Philadelphia in 2025 and traded from Green Bay to Miami in August for a 2028 sixth-round pick, he now gets his second start back in upstate New York — against a defense that has not surrendered a touchdown since the first quarter of November, per the Democrat and Chronicle.

Here is the part of this story that is actually about Buffalo, though: the defense that built that streak came out of the Jets game limping. Cornerback Christian Benford was ruled out with a groin injury in the fourth quarter after entering the game questionable with the right wrist injury he suffered against Minnesota, per the Democrat and Chronicle; Benford has 33 tackles and eight pass breakups in eight games this season, per the same reporting. Nickel cornerback Dee Alford was evaluated for a concussion twice, was cleared to return once, then was ruled out, and must clear the NFL's concussion protocol before he can play against Miami, per the same reporting. Linebacker Dorian Williams left in the fourth quarter with a calf injury and did not return — after recording a team-high nine tackles, two quarterback hits, a pass defended and his first career sack, per the Democrat and Chronicle. Safety Cole Bishop had his right arm and shoulder examined late but played 68 of 71 defensive snaps with no injury designation announced, per the same reporting; cornerback Maxwell Hairston was shaken up late and walked off under his own power, and linebackers Terrel Bernard and Joe Andreessen both headed to the X-ray room after the game, per The Buffalo News via the Democrat and Chronicle, with neither receiving an in-game designation. The one full-strength debut helped: safety Amani Hooker, five days after being acquired from Tennessee, played all 71 defensive snaps against the Jets with seven tackles and a pass defensed, per AP. Wednesday's first practice report of Dolphins week is the first real clue about who is actually available — and until it posts, every one of those names is a report, not a ruling.

Miami's own list is longer, and it explains how McCord got this job. The Dolphins placed starting quarterback Malik Willis on injured reserve on Nov. 10 with an injury that originated in his groin and progressed to his core; the earliest he can return is Week 14, per the Democrat and Chronicle. Running back De'Von Achane suffered a torn ACL on Sept. 27 and will miss the rest of the season, and defensive lineman Zach Sieler was placed on injured reserve Nov. 10 and is also out for the season, per the same reporting — three of Miami's six original team captains are on injured reserve. Miami will also arrive with a brand-new kicker: the Dolphins waived Zane Gonzalez on Monday, one day after he missed field goals from 47 and 51 yards and an extra point in the 24-22 loss at Indianapolis, per Reuters via Field Level Media, which noted Miami is looking for its third placekicker of the season. A 1-8 team, on its backup quarterback and its third kicker, walking into Highmark Stadium in late November — that is the matchup. On paper.

The paper, however, is not the prize. The Associated Press reported that Buffalo need not apologize for the caliber of its competition, and that clinching a sixth division title in seven years seems a matter of when, not if, given the state of the AFC East's quarterback ranks — a picture that got clearer Monday, when Patriots starter Drake Maye was believed to have suffered a long-term lower leg injury that will reportedly sideline him for several weeks and possibly the rest of the season, per the Democrat and Chronicle, with New England already trailing Buffalo by four games in the loss column. What is still unanswered, per AP, is how Buffalo stacks up against the league's contenders — and those answers start arriving immediately after Miami: a five-week stretch that opens with Kansas City at home on Thanksgiving night and ends with a Christmas Day game at Denver, with trips to New England and Green Bay and a home game against Chicago in between, all against teams that entered Week 11 at .500 or better, per AP. Josh Allen said it himself after the Jets win, per AP: "We're not playing our best football right now." So Sunday's job is twofold — extend a touchdown-less streak that is now older than some of the quarterbacks it has faced, and get the secondary that has to survive Mahomes, Love, Williams and Nix through the afternoon healthy enough to try. Handle McCord, protect the streak, and let the real exam start on Thanksgiving. Go Bills — and get every Dolphins-week practice report in your inbox every morning with The BNC Blitz.

body: The final score says the Buffalo Bills beat the New York Jets 31-12 on Sunday at MetLife Stadium, and the standings say Buffalo is 8-1 — its best start since 1991, per the Associated Press — with five straight wins and its first AFC East victory of the season, per the Bills' official recap. Film Room is here to tell you the score is burying the lede. The real number from Sunday is 33: dating back to the first half of the Week 8 win over Baltimore, Buffalo has now gone 33 consecutive defensive drives without allowing a touchdown, per the Bills' official recap — the longest active streak in the NFL and the franchise's longest since the 1999 season. Three weeks ago this defense was the problem with this team. Right now it is the story of this team.

Start with what Sunday actually looked like on tape. The Jets moved the ball — 376 total yards, per the New York Post's report card — and it bought them four Jason Sanders field goals and nothing else. New York reached the red zone twice and came away without a touchdown both times, per the Bills' official recap, and went 3-for-13 on third down, per the Post. Buffalo recorded four sacks, 12 quarterback hits and two takeaways, per the Democrat and Chronicle's 11-stats breakdown. And this is no longer a one-game heater: since the Week 7 bye, Buffalo is allowing the second-fewest yards per play on third down in the league (2.4), with opponents converting at just a 17.6 percent clip, and the ninth-fewest yards per play inside the red zone (2.3), per the Bills' official recap. Defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard's unit is not surviving drives anymore. It is ending them — early, and then again at the goal line.

The quarterback film tells the physical half of the story. Geno Smith finished 13-of-21 for 148 yards, per the Democrat and Chronicle, and Buffalo knocked him out of the game twice: first late in the first half, when he was hit high by linebacker Terrel Bernard and low by rookie edge rusher T.J. Parker and went into concussion evaluation, per the Democrat and Chronicle's live coverage, and then again in the third quarter on a blitz hit by safety Cole Bishop that left him with an ankle injury, per the New York Post. In between and after, rookie Cade Klubnik took his first career NFL snaps and finished 11-of-20 for 137 yards and an interception, per Reuters. Parker sacked his former Clemson teammate twice in a span of three plays in the fourth quarter, per the Democrat and Chronicle; rookie cornerback Davison Igbinosun intercepted Klubnik (then fumbled the return back, because even this defense's highlights come with a footnote); and when a Jets hook-and-lateral backfired late, rookie linebacker Kaleb Elarms-Orr recovered the fumble that set up the dagger. Per Buffalo Rumblings' recap, new safety Amani Hooker was an instant upgrade in his Bills debut, too. This is what a connected defense looks like: the pressure, the coverage and the blitz are all arriving from different names on the same snap.

The people inside it keep pointing at the same word: communication. "The communication has been at a high level," Bernard said, per the Bills' official recap, describing a unit where, in his words, you do not see guys running free while the defensive line gets home. Head coach Joe Brady went further, calling Sunday, per the same recap, "the best win we've had this season" — not because of the margin, but because of the week: a physical Monday night game in Minnesota, a return home in the early hours of Tuesday morning, and then straight back on the road for a division game. "There were so many excuses that could have been had this week and it's just not who they are," Brady said, per the Bills' recap. When a head coach calls a 19-point win over a 2-8 team his best of the year, he is not talking about the opponent. He is talking about the standard — and right now the defense is the unit setting it.

Then there is the second half, which is where the film turns from a grind into a sprint. Buffalo averaged just 4.3 yards per play in a first half that ended 10-6, per Buffalo Rumblings, and actually trailed in feel if not on the board when the Jets cut it to 10-9 early in the third quarter. What followed, per the Bills' official recap, was 21 points on 16 plays for 230 yards — an average of 14.4 yards per play in the second half, per Rumblings — built on scoring drives of four plays, two plays and one play, per head coach Joe Brady in the team recap. The four explosive gains did the damage: a 54-yard strike to Dalton Kincaid, the longest reception of his career, per the Bills' recap; a 21-yard James Cook run; a 45-yard touchdown bomb to DJ Moore — the healthy, off-the-injury-report version this site wrote about Saturday, catching four balls for 90 yards; and the 74-yard Cook touchdown that ended the afternoon. The Democrat and Chronicle's stat breakdown put it cleanest: Buffalo scored three second-half touchdowns on seven plays. Seven.

Cook's closer deserves its own paragraph, because the record book is starting to follow him around. He finished with 18 carries for 157 yards at 8.7 yards a pop, per Bills Wire, and the 74-yarder was the longest touchdown run of his career, hit 21.56 miles per hour on Next Gen Stats, produced 75 rushing yards over expected, and was Buffalo's longest rushing touchdown since LeSean McCoy's 75-yarder in 2016, per Bills Wire and the Bills' official recap. Per the Democrat and Chronicle's 11-stats breakdown, Cook is now just the fifth player in NFL history with at least 75 rushing yards and a rushing touchdown in eight consecutive games — a streak Bills PR, via Yardbarker, notes ties the longest such run since LaDainian Tomlinson in 2006. He sits second in the NFL in rushing yards through Week 10, per the Bills' recap. And Josh Allen quietly rewrote another line above him: 11-of-21 for 196 yards with a touchdown pass, an interception and two 1-yard rushing touchdowns, per the Democrat and Chronicle — enough to pass Peyton Manning for the most total touchdowns by a player through his first 10 seasons, with 323, per the Bills' official recap, a record Allen set in his ninth season. His review of the offense afterward, per the team recap: "We're not playing our best football right now." An 8-1 team whose quarterback says that out loud is a problem for everybody else.

Film Room keeps the receipts, so here are Sunday's costs, reported as they were reported. Cornerback Christian Benford, who entered the day questionable with a wrist injury, was ruled out during the game with a groin injury, per the Democrat and Chronicle. Nickel cornerback Dee Alford left in the second half with a concussion after being evaluated for a head injury and cleared to return earlier in the game, per the Associated Press via TSN. Linebacker Dorian Williams injured a calf in the fourth quarter, per the same AP report, and cornerback Maxwell Hairston was shaken up late before returning, per the Democrat and Chronicle. Buffalo also committed nine pre-snap penalties, seven of them accepted, per Athlon Sports' recap of the Locked On Bills discussion — the sloppiness Allen was talking about is on the film, too. None of those names has a designation yet; the week's first practice report will start that conversation. Next up, Buffalo finally comes home: the Miami Dolphins at Highmark Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 PM ET, per Bills Wire. The defense has not allowed a touchdown in 33 drives, the offense can now score three touchdowns in seven plays, and the Bills are 8-1 for the first time in 35 years. January football is being built in November, one drive at a time. Go Bills — and get the full Dolphins-week breakdown in your inbox every morning with The BNC Blitz.
